Response Get Watchlist V1 Watchlist Get
Response List Reports V1 Reports Get
Response List Runs V1 Runs Get

get.description:
Server-sent events: `status`, `progress`, `node` and a final `end`. A client that
reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=`, for a fresh `EventSource`) receives
only what it missed.

averages.title: Averages
averages.description: Simple moving averages (sma20, sma50, sma200), one value per bar

target_claim_id.title: Target Claim Id
target_claim_id.description: The claim ID you dispute, e.g. C-bull-1-2.

kind.description: fact = reported figure or event; calculation = derived number; interpretation = reasoned judgement; scenario = conditional possibility.

evidence_ids.title: Evidence Ids
evidence_ids.description: IDs from the evidence pack (e.g. F3, M12, A2). Facts and calculations need at least one. Never invent an ID.

Coverage.title: Coverage
Coverage.description: Availability of one source category for a run (docs/05, "Freshness and coverage").

DerivedMetric.title: DerivedMetric
DerivedMetric.description: A value computed in Python from stored inputs. Reproducible from `inputs`.

impact.title: Impact
impact.description: -2 clearly negative, -1, 0 neutral, +1, +2 clearly positive for the company's prospects.

materiality.title: Materiality
materiality.description: How much the event matters relative to the company's size.

EvidencePack.title: EvidencePack
EvidencePack.description: Everything a run may cite, frozen before interpretation starts.

Factor.title: Factor
Factor.description:
One rule's contribution to a pillar score, with the evidence it read.

Rules in the same group read the same underlying move, so a group's total is
capped; the cap shows up as its own factor (`kind="cap"`) so the factors still add
up to the score.

FinancialFact.title: FinancialFact
FinancialFact.description: A reported figure, stored in base units (INR, not crore) with its reporting context.

Horizon.title: Horizon
Horizon.description: The three outlook horizons every report scores.

adjustment.title: Adjustment
adjustment.description: Between -5 and +5 points on the draft score, only where the debate or risk reviews show it misses something material. Usually 0.

drivers.title: Drivers
drivers.description: What most drives this horizon's view, one short line each.

up_if.title: Up If
up_if.description: Observable events that would raise the signal.

down_if.title: Down If
down_if.description: Observable events that would lower the signal.

IndexSeries.title: IndexSeries
IndexSeries.description: An NSE index the stock is compared with: daily closes and its published P/E.

Level.title: Level
Level.description: A price the stock turned from or traded heavily at before. Not a target.

Pillar.title: Pillar
Pillar.description: One scored area of the research. Each belongs to the analyst that reviews it.

PillarScore.title: PillarScore
PillarScore.description: A 0-100 score for one area. Every area starts at 50 (no lean either way).

PriceBar.title: PriceBar
PriceBar.description: One end-of-day bar. Provider and adjustment basis are part of its identity.

PriceRange.title: PriceRange
PriceRange.description:
How far the price has typically moved, or what stated scenarios imply. Not a
forecast.

cutoff.title: Cutoff
cutoff.description: Knowledge cutoff; None means the latest completed data.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: Are the draft scores too optimistic (too_high), fair, or too pessimistic (too_low) given the risks you see?

constraints.title: Constraints
constraints.description: Conditions that should hold before relying on the signal.

pillar.description: The code-computed score you are adjusting (your own).

points.title: Points
points.description: Between -15 and +15. Code clamps anything outside.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: One sentence: what the scoring rules missed.

SignalFlip.title: SignalFlip
SignalFlip.description:
The nearest next-session close that would change a horizon's signal, with
every other input held as it is.

SourceRef.title: SourceRef
SourceRef.description: Where a piece of evidence came from and when it became public.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: Two or three plain sentences a non-expert understands.

Veto.title: Veto
Veto.description:
A code-enforced constraint. `block` withholds every signal; `cap` holds each
horizon's score at Neutral or below. A persuasive narrative cannot lift either.
